text.p: The brokerage arm of Macquarie Bank Ltd, Macquarie Equities Ltd, said it has upgraded its earnings forecast for West Australian Newspapers Holdings Ltd (WAN), by seven percent to A$59.4 million for the year to June 30, 1997 and recommended the stock as a strong buy.

In its September equities round-up, Macquarie said the upgrade was based on WAN having past the bottom of its cycle and now being in growth mode. "The 1997 earnings upgrade of seven percent could be conservative, given that our revenue growth forecast appears on the low side," the report said.
The report said the stock, at the time of publication was trading at a seven percent premium to the All Ordinaries index compared to a traditional premium of up to 15 percent.

"Part of the reason for the consistent WAN outperformance is the stronger West Australian state growth compared with the rest of Australia," the report said. "Since newspaper profits are highly correlated to economic activity, West Australia with stronger growth than the rest of Australia continues to outperform, and so does WAN."
Macquarie said another factor impacting WAN's earnings was lower newsprint costs which provided a solid base for continued strong profit growth.
At 11.40 a.m. (0140 GMT), WAN shares were two cents weaker at A$4.90.
At the time the report was written, WAN shares were trading at A$4.93.
